# mini-py - for agents

> **This document owns:** the commands that build, test, run and lint mini-py, the conventions an agent cannot infer from the code, and the gotchas. Forty lines at most; the docs index holds everything else. *(draft, review me)*

## Commands

- install: `pip install -e .` [pyproject.toml]

## Conventions

- open question: branch, commit and PR rules an agent would get wrong without being told

## Gotchas

- open question: the thing that costs an afternoon here

## Docs

- [docs/INDEX.md](docs/INDEX.md) - the map; read it before the folder.

docs/INDEX.md.content:
# mini-py docs

> A small Python service fixture. Deliberately has no docs folder.

Pick the one file you need here; do not read the folder. Every doc says what it owns under its title; a fact has one home and the other docs link to it. State is one of `skeleton`, `draft`, `unreviewed`, `reviewed YYYY-MM-DD`, `stale YYYY-MM-DD`.

## Getting started

- [Setup](getting-started/SETUP.md): the path from a clean machine to a first visible success - prerequisites, install, run, what success looks like, and what to do when it fails. - skeleton
- [Onboarding](getting-started/ONBOARDING.md): the reading order for a new person, the path per role, and the vocabulary this repository uses. - skeleton

## Guides

- [Development](DEVELOPMENT.md): the daily loop of changing code here - branch, run, debug, lint, test, open a pull request. - skeleton

## Reference

- [Architecture](reference/ARCHITECTURE.md): the map of the system - its context, the containers it runs as, the building blocks inside them, how a request moves at runtime, how it is deployed, and the qualities and risks that shaped it. Decisions live in their own records. - skeleton
- [Data model](reference/DATA_MODEL.md): the tables and their meaning — what each one stores, what is append-only, and the conventions every migration follows. - skeleton
- [API reference](reference/API.md): the endpoints — path, method, auth, request and response shape, errors. The API is the contract; nobody reimplements it. - skeleton
- [CLI reference](reference/CLI.md): the commands this repository exposes — each command, its arguments and flags, and what it does. - skeleton

## Explanation

- [Product](PRODUCT.md): what the product is, who it is for, where it is going, and what it has said no to. - skeleton

<!-- docs-structure: start here -->
## Start here

Three files, in this order. Everything else is one hop from the second one.

1. **This file** - what mini-py is and how the repository is laid out.
2. **[docs/INDEX.md](docs/INDEX.md)** - the index of every doc: what each one owns and its state. Pick the one file you need there; do not read the folder.
3. **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)** - the commands and conventions a coding agent or a new contributor needs, forty lines at most.

The docs a reader starts with are still skeletons; the index says which. The index says which file is which; this README keeps no list of its own, so the two cannot drift.

The docs have a shape and a checker: one index, five buckets by what a reader came to do, an owner line on every doc, no line-number citations. `docs_structure.py --repo .` from the docs-structure skill checks it; `docs/structure.json` is its manifest.
<!-- /docs-structure: start here -->
